title: Insurance Restoration — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Field worksheets for working to the IICRC standards, pricing mitigation so it gets paid, mastering Xactimate line items, supplementing roof claims, negotiating with adjusters and public adjusters, and deciding whether TPA programs deserve a place in the business

worksheets.title: Standard-of-Care and Mitigation Billing Audit
worksheets.purpose: Hold every water and mold job to the S500 and S520 standard of care, prove containment and dryness with readings instead of fan-days, and price mitigation with one consistent protocol that changes pricing but never scope.
instructions: Complete this worksheet on site, before demolition starts, and update it every monitoring visit until the drying file is closed.
Write actual readings, model numbers, dollar amounts and dates, never estimates from memory or round guesses made in the truck.
Treat every 'should' in the standard as the standard of care, and log each deviation the moment it happens.
Price the job with the same naming, bundling and pricing protocol you used on the last claim, with no exceptions.
Reconcile billed equipment against photos and equipment logs before the estimate or invoice leaves the office.

fields.name: containment_pressure_log
fields.prompt: Record the containment setup for your current mold job: poly thickness and type, the manometer reading in pascals, and the time the reading was taken. State whether demolition or air movers started before the containment held its target pressure.
fields.example: Containment built with 6 mil fire-retardant poly around the hall bath; manometer held -5 Pa at 9:40 a.m. before any drywall came down, the crucial metric proving containment works [Balanced Building Biology — YdUmzaa5wO0 @ 00:02:47]. No demo and no air movers ran until that reading was logged and photographed beside the manometer display.

fields.name: removal_method
fields.prompt: Describe how mold-affected material on this job will be removed. Confirm physical removal is the method, name any product someone proposed to fog or bleach with, and explain why that proposal was rejected in your written scope.
fields.example: Homeowner asked whether we could just bleach the closet wall. Written scope states physical removal of affected drywall and HEPA vacuuming, because proper remediation is about physical removal [Phill McGurk — Dl8DpDk97_A @ 00:03:11] and bleach is essentially a masking agent [Balanced Building Biology — YdUmzaa5wO0 @ 00:04:41]. No fogging line appears anywhere on the estimate.

fields.name: condition_and_category
fields.prompt: Classify the job by Condition 1, 2 or 3 rather than visible square footage, and note the water category with the reasoning. If the source is a drain or sewer line, state where it originated relative to the trap.
fields.example: Kitchen sink backup: water originated beyond the trap, so it is logged as category three, since if it originates from beyond the trap it's category three [TheIICRC — bcid0F9jRTI @ 00:15:07]. Cabinet toe-kick and adjacent drywall classed by Condition rather than the small visible stain, with the reasoning written into the file before demolition began.

fields.name: deviation_record
fields.prompt: List every point where this job departs from a 'should' in the standard. For each, record how it was documented, which affected parties were told, and whether the owner gave written authorization, noting any limitation an adjuster tried to impose.
fields.example: Adjuster asked us to skip removing wet baseboard. Logged as a deviation, communicated to the owner and tenant, and held until the owner signed written authorization; an adjuster cannot impose limitations [Time's Dark Captains — y00Yi4bnLx4 @ 00:12:13]. The standard is voluntary, but in front of a judge or jury, skipping it loses [TheIICRC — JOiWfXdUwjM @ 00:14:53].

fields.name: moisture_monitoring
fields.prompt: Record your moisture monitoring plan: the meter model and serial used, reading spacing, and daily readings. Confirm the same meter stays on the job from first reading to close, and state the readings that justify closing the drying file.
fields.example: Readings taken every 5 ft along the affected wall with one meter, serial logged on day one, because the restorer should use the same meter throughout a project [Coach8 — 7gZTdFWoHgs @ 00:37:15]. File closed on day-four readings matching the dry goal, not on fan-days; three or four days of fans does not prove the house is dry [Andrew Melrose — iQ4PIKW3sEc @ 00:02:41].

fields.name: equipment_placement
fields.prompt: Calculate air mover placement for the affected area: one per room, one per 50-70 square feet of floor, one per 100-150 square feet of wall above 2 ft, and one per offset over 18 inches. Show the math.
fields.example: Darren Floyd's worked example lands a 750 square foot loss at 12 to 16 air movers [APPALeadership — cPAFOZbMKQE @ 00:42:22]. Our 740 square foot basement: three rooms, floor share, wall share above 2 ft and two offsets gave 14 units. Before placing, we pulled water off the top and underneath before mats went down [Restoration Technical Institute — XMpZ-8ZsSW8 @ 00:01:43].

fields.name: filtration_and_air
fields.prompt: Document the air filtration device filter stack in use, replacement costs for each stage, and where the unit exhausts. Confirm negative air is not being drawn from a crawlspace and note any furnace backdraft risk you checked.
fields.example: AFD stack: pre-filter at $8-12, secondary at $15-20, HEPA at about $153 capturing 99.97% at 0.3 microns, carbon added for odor [APPALeadership — cPAFOZbMKQE @ 00:29:36]. Unit exhausts out the laundry window. Crawlspace hatch stays sealed; no negative air drawn from it because of furnace backdraft risk flagged alongside the filter stack.

fields.name: truck_roll_pricing
fields.prompt: Price this job against your minimum revenue per truck roll. Count every planned visit, including sell, drop, monitoring and pickup trips, then state the floor price you will quote if the customer is paying cash rather than through insurance.
fields.example: Small cash-pay laundry room leak: sell/drop visit plus equipment pickup already puts us near $800-$1,000 before work, since every time your truck rolls you need to make at least four to five hundred bucks [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — 72Qh6dRR94U @ 00:02:07]. Quoted at the $2,000 floor, with a $489 assess-and-reposition charge [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — m97k7TBcJgY @ 00:05:45].

fields.name: pricing_protocol
fields.prompt: Write down the single naming, bundling and pricing protocol you run on every claim, including equipment-day roundup, truck mount hourly rate and category pricing. Confirm you changed only pricing, never scope, and reconciled billed equipment against photos and logs.
fields.example: Equipment days billed as 3.6 instead of 3 on every fan, dehu and scrubber [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — roHp-ZzbYvs @ 00:07:49]; truck mount at $189 per committed hour. Eight air movers on the draft, six verified in photos, so the field team was asked before submission [ReconSmart Solutions LLC — 3DF6Xf4wlIg @ 00:08:54]. Change your pricing not the scope.

fields.name: reductions_and_payment_terms
fields.prompt: Record how you will handle adjuster reductions and slow payment on this file: the streamline discount ceiling you will offer, the F9 notes explaining charges, and the deposit, payment schedule and late-fee terms on any self-pay mitigation contract.
fields.example: Adjuster flagged eleven lines. Instead of arguing each, we asked for the total and offered a streamline discount capped at 10 percent for immediate payment [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — roHp-ZzbYvs @ 00:11:38]. Self-pay side: deposit, thirds schedule, 5 percent late fee at 30 days and an attorney letter at 120 days [On The Job with Jason Peters — h3bbJRR6ceA @ 00:17:06].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not demolish or start air movers until containment holds -5 Pa on a manometer, do not close the drying file on fan-days instead of same-meter readings, do not deviate without written owner authorization, and do not submit until billed equipment matches photos and logs.

worksheets.title: Xactimate Line-Item and Roof Supplement Builder
worksheets.purpose: Build estimates that start from the highest supportable position, catch money hidden in Click-for-Detail and commonly missed items, and rebuild short roof scopes line by line with photos, measurements and notes that prove rather than complain.
instructions: Reprice after every macro load and after each monthly price list update before the estimate leaves your desk.
Open Click-for-Detail on every window line and every newly added line item before accepting the default price.
Check every quantity against the photo set and the sketch, never against memory of the walkthrough.
Photograph every tear-off discovery before it is covered, with wide shot, close shot, measurement and labeled roof location.
Address supplements to corporate or inside claims and explain the supplement to the homeowner before the build begins.

fields.name: price_list_and_reprice
fields.prompt: Note the Xactimate price list month loaded on this estimate, the date you last repriced, and every macro dropped in. Record the dollar change after repricing so you can see what a stale price list would have cost.
fields.example: Estimate opened on the April list, repriced after the May 2026 update and after the bathroom macro loaded, per the reprice-before-sending rule [Claim Daddy — Qu-NqEwWWPk @ 02:40:15]. Overhead And Profit added $2,688.91 by repricing one open estimate after North Texas increases [Overhead And Profit — A7SLk2mjCXU @ 00:03:14]; ours moved $1,140.

fields.name: click_for_detail_review
fields.prompt: List every window line and newly added line item where you opened Click-for-Detail. For each, note what the default includes or excludes, such as low-E glass, and the dollar difference after correcting the selection to match the actual material.
fields.example: Two single-hung vinyl windows in the rear bedroom. Click-for-Detail showed the default excludes low-E glass; the installed units have it. Estimate Mastery reports $225 left off one window line because the writer never read the detail [Estimate Mastery — WNR0K0ubIoI @ 00:01:06]. Both lines corrected, with a photo of the installed glass attached as support.

fields.name: commonly_missed_items
fields.prompt: Check this estimate against the commonly missed items and list which ones apply: detach-and-reset appliances, project management, anti-microbial, haul-off and drying equipment unit-days. For each item added, write the quantity and the reason it belongs on this file.
fields.example: Added detach-and-reset on the refrigerator and range, anti-microbial on exposed framing, haul-off for demolished cabinets, and project management at the Dallas residential rate near $70 an hour. Drying equipment billed per 24-hour unit-day. Asked for project management even on mitigation-only, since I'd rather ask and be turned down than to not ask at all [Daughtry Construction Group — HLwvN9mF1R0 @ 00:06:37].

fields.name: sketch_and_quantities
fields.prompt: Describe how the sketch drives quantities on this file. Record room dimensions, wall and ceiling repair quantities, and how you converted patch areas into sheets. Confirm every quantity was checked against photos rather than memory before the estimate went out.
fields.example: Hall ceiling sketched at 12 by 10; the stain needed a patch of 32, which equals one 4x8 sheet, so the line reads one sheet, not a partial. Every quantity was rechecked against the photo set, because the rule is never go off strictly off your memory and always review your photos [Claim Daddy — Qu-NqEwWWPk @ 01:17:58].

fields.name: footnotes_and_f9
fields.prompt: Write the F9 notes for removal and replacement lines that are likely to be questioned, including any vanity detach item priced above plain removal. Each note should explain why the item was chosen, its quantity and how the work will be performed.
fields.example: Vanity detach line carries an F9 note justifying thoughtful extraction to save the stone top [Actionable — s4xCprLX1Yw @ 00:05:15]. Both removal and replacement lines are footnoted, following Chad Michael's 206-page estimate that works as a database the adjuster reviews item by item [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — Lh586v6HcYw @ 00:14:59].

fields.name: bid_items_and_utilities
fields.prompt: List any bid items on this estimate, such as electricity consumption or new mini-split pricing. Record the documents supporting each one, including three months of utility bills, and the price change from the prior month's list where it applies.
fields.example: Electricity-consumption bid item held until three months of utility bills were in the file, because Shelter denied utilities on a DP-6 rental [Actionable — s4xCprLX1Yw @ 00:08:26]. One-zone mini-split repriced from $1,500 in April to $4,200 in May 2026; in April you were not making money on mini-splits [Actionable — s4xCprLX1Yw @ 00:19:55].

fields.name: adjuster_pushback_opener
fields.prompt: Script your first response when the adjuster pushes back on this estimate. Write the exact opening question, the starting position you are defending, and the code reasons stacked behind your most contested line items before the conversation turns to dollars.
fields.example: Opening line, verbatim: which item or items in the estimate did you have a problem with [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — Lh586v6HcYw @ 00:16:44]. Position held from the top, since they push down at all times and you start from the highest position to end there [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — Lh586v6HcYw @ 00:14:28]. Expect one-coat defaults on white ceilings.

fields.name: tearoff_documentation
fields.prompt: Record each tear-off discovery photographed before it was covered. For every item, list the wide shot, close shot, measurement and labeled roof location, and match the measurement report to the actual building before the supplement goes out.
fields.example: Rotted decking found at the north eave: wide shot, close shot, tape measurement and slope label captured before new sheathing went down [American Roof Supplements — TkCEjbO6vQs @ 00:07:23]. Measurement report rechecked because measurement reports must match the building [American Roof Supplements — DR03Zlogfe0 @ 00:01:26]. That is the difference between complaining and proving.

fields.name: supplement_routing_and_lines
fields.prompt: List each line changed from the carrier's original scope, the bolded note explaining the change, and where the supplement is addressed. Note any small items you will concede for rapport and whether one interior water spot unlocks overhead and profit.
fields.example: Supplement sent to inside claims, not the field adjuster who wrote the scope [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — bVX2IRINNSM @ 00:00:30]. Each changed line carries a note explaining why it differs from the original statement of loss. Drip edge conceded rather than argued for an hour; a closet water spot keeps O&P alive [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — bVX2IRINNSM @ 00:43:18].

fields.name: homeowner_supplement_conversation
fields.prompt: Write how and when the supplement is explained to the homeowner, the protection-from-surprises framing you use, and the decking decision. State whether decking was approved before the build or which mid-job emergency documentation plan covers the risk.
fields.example: Supplement explained at color selection as protection from financial surprises, with no payment promised [The STRONG Roofer w/ Adam Bensman — zxGa72oAf0w @ 00:02:17]. Decking was not approved pre-build, so the mid-job photo plan and accepted risk are signed off [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — 4dhIe6HGIs0 @ 00:38:28]. Necessary replacement does not automatically mean covered replacement.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not send the estimate or supplement until it is repriced on the current price list, Click-for-Detail is checked on every window and new line, every tear-off discovery is photographed before cover, the file is addressed to inside claims, and the homeowner has heard the supplement explained.

worksheets.title: Adjuster Negotiation and TPA Program Readiness Plan
worksheets.purpose: Read the carrier estimate as a weak baseline, negotiate scope and pricing without crossing into coverage, decide when a public adjuster belongs on the claim, and test whether TPA program work earns its fees before the first assignment lands.
instructions: Read the carrier's first estimate line by line before any phone call, marking squares, quantities, units and trade codes.
Discuss scope and pricing only; route every coverage question to the homeowner, their agent or a licensed adjuster.
Calendar proof-of-loss and recoverable depreciation deadlines on the day of loss, not the day the paperwork arrives.
Ask whether every extra adjuster demand is a recommendation or a requirement, and what any requirement is based on.
Model program fees, lost markup and drying caps in dollars before signing any administrator contract or vendor agreement.

fields.name: carrier_estimate_read
fields.prompt: Read the carrier's first estimate line by line. Record roofing squares, tear-off quantities, any unit-entry errors, and removal items coded to the wrong trade. Note how far the carrier number sits from your bid before any negotiation starts.
fields.example: Carrier wrote 0.33 squares, which basically means one bundle of shingles to repair the roof [Builder's Perspective Public Adjusting — kWxJ6PIkM-M @ 00:04:42]. Area entered as 24.48 SF where 2,448 SF was measured. Removal lines coded DMO; switched to trade codes, which Chad Michael reports approved about 40 percent of the time [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — vkrXTVQcVQQ @ 00:13:50].

fields.name: tearoff_separate_lines
fields.prompt: List every item the carrier folded into shingle tear-off that must be written as its own line, such as drip edge and flashing. Also note any continuous flooring run that extends beyond the room where the water stopped.
fields.example: Tear-off only pays dump fees, hauling, disposal and removal labor, so drip edge and step flashing went on separate lines [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — vkrXTVQcVQQ @ 00:08:43]. Inside, the laminate runs from the kitchen through the dining room with no threshold, so the carrier owes the continuous run [Builder's Perspective Public Adjusting — kWxJ6PIkM-M @ 00:11:31].

fields.name: negotiation_call_plan
fields.prompt: Outline the adjuster call: the question list you will run, the discount ceiling you will accept, and what happens to the undisputed amount if reductions exceed that ceiling. Keep the call short and refuse to argue individual line items emotionally.
fields.example: Three-to-four-minute call from the question list; reductions up to 10 percent accepted, anything deeper refused and the undisputed amount collected [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — 3xfQ7PdL-AA @ 00:06:23]. No line-by-line fight, because they are simply arguing line items to get you heated and it just doesn't do any good [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — 3xfQ7PdL-AA @ 00:08:28].

fields.name: adjuster_demand_check
fields.prompt: For every extra demand the adjuster makes, record whether you asked if it is a recommendation or a requirement, and if required, what it is based on. Note how you phrased your evidence without definitive claims or appeals to tenure.
fields.example: Adjuster requested an additional inspection. Asked whether it was a recommendation or a requirement, then what it was based on [Chris Zimmerman — 9A5QEe9xxXk @ 00:01:21]; answer was recommendation, so it was declined. Reply used 'evidence suggests' instead of definitive claims, with no mention of file count, since that is really not relevant to the file [Chris Zimmerman — LwNOcenSP_c @ 00:03:42].

fields.name: coverage_boundary_and_contract
fields.prompt: Confirm your contract states a scope and price with a cancellation clause and a change order for partial approval. Record where your role stops at scope and pricing, and how coverage questions are handed to the homeowner or a licensed adjuster.
fields.example: Old contract read 'we will do the work for the amount the insurance company approves'; rewritten with stated scope, price, cancellation clause and partial-approval change order [Building Experts Institute — RmjqTZJ3II0 @ 00:01:19]. No homeowner permission or power of attorney used to negotiate, since Texas section 4102.163 bars it [Daly & Black, P.C. — jaGktNyKvE4 @ 00:01:55]. You need a license for that.

fields.name: deadlines_and_settlement
fields.prompt: Record the date of loss, the proof-of-loss deadline calendared that same day, and the recoverable depreciation clock. Note any newly discovered damage that restarts that clock, and confirm you have not agreed to settle at any stage.
fields.example: Proof-of-loss calendared on the day of loss at 30 days, the short end of the range [The Adjuster's Roundtable — _wmRAji2ZmI @ 00:08:35]. Hidden decking damage found at tear-off restarts the 180-day RD clock, since no claim is ever closed until all repairs have actually been made and paid for [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — vkrXTVQcVQQ @ 00:23:30].

fields.name: public_adjuster_decision
fields.prompt: Decide whether a public adjuster belongs on this claim. Record the fee tier offered, how the fee affects the repair budget, and whether your company will work alongside the PA or decline, citing the reasoning from each side.
fields.example: PA offered at the 10 percent tier; Vince Perri reports no issue in 9 of 10 roofer-referred cases [Public Adjuster Show with Vince Perri — RRn3mzn9xCw @ 00:15:09] and says a PA puts more money in pocket 10 times out of 10. Weighed against FirehouseEducation's never-deal-with-PAs stance and an insurer-side lawyer's warning that the fee can leave repairs short.

fields.name: tpa_program_economics
fields.prompt: Model the economics of joining a TPA program on this job type. Record the program fee percentage, the markup you lose against your standard list, the drying-day cap, and whether guaranteed volume still leaves a profitable job after paperwork.
fields.example: Program charges 5 to 10 percent to do the work [Water Damage Restoration Coach - Jon Schoen — -0hAYhkhJaw @ 00:02:35], and the preset list kills our 20 percent markup. Drying capped at 3 days. Brian Close's warning that guaranteed work is not always profitable is weighed against David Smith's $250,000 fire nobody chased [The DYOJO (The DYOJO) — onSDIprTeAU @ 00:11:17].

fields.name: program_equipment_and_software
fields.prompt: Before the first program job, record the equipment counts the program's day-stamped report calls for, your Xactimate seats and any second software, and who handles the double documentation upload: trained admin staff or a subcontracted paperwork service.
fields.example: Pulled the program's equipment counts before placing dehus, because an oversized unit gets paid as the small one the room called for [Water Damage Restoration Coach - Jon Schoen — -0hAYhkhJaw @ 00:06:02]. Two Xactimate seats confirmed; admin trained in-house for the double upload, since it's documentation, documentation, documentation regardless of the end user [The DYOJO (The DYOJO) — onSDIprTeAU @ 00:48:01].

fields.name: program_access_and_risk
fields.prompt: Record your plan for getting on and staying on the program list: the regional manager contact, adjusters or agents pushing for you, subs ready for volume, and your contract redlines. State what share of revenue this single channel may carry.
fields.example: Regional manager invited to inspect our warehouse, name and number saved for the introduction [Water Damage Restoration Coach - Jon Schoen — -0hAYhkhJaw @ 00:11:42]. Two hungry subs lined up for overflow. Program work capped as one channel among several, because a shop built around 150 jobs a year collapsed to one job a month in 2008 [The DYOJO — onSDIprTeAU @ 00:59:09].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not get on the phone with the adjuster until the carrier estimate is read line by line, deadlines are calendared, and the contract states scope and price; do not sign a program agreement until fees, lost markup and drying caps are modeled and the contract is redlined.

worksheets.title: Fire, Smoke, Contents Documentation and the Plumber Referral Engine
worksheets.purpose: Turn every fire, smoke and contents job into a defensible, billable file built from the first site visit, then build a plumber referral engine that feeds steady water work through discovery, disciplined free dry-outs and a call-handling system that closes inbound leads.
instructions: Fill in every field while the job is live, using your own photos, scans, readings and notices rather than memory, because you get paid for what you document.
Identify the smoke type with a sponge test on a 1 ft x 1 ft square before writing any cleaning labor, and record the multiplier you applied.
Never discard an owner's belongings on your own call, never ozone damp, wet or soft goods, and put humidity readings and no-warranty notices in writing.
For the plumber fields, run discovery before any pitch: find out what each service plumber wants, profile them in your CRM, and track jobs sent over 90 days.
Review this worksheet with your project manager and your sales lead each week, and update the free dry-out ledger and close rate before the next referral visit.

fields.name: smoke_type_and_cleaning_multiplier
fields.prompt: Identify the smoke type on your current fire job before you bid it. Record whether the residue is wet or dry, how you confirmed it, and what cleaning-time multiplier you are applying to the labor lines in the estimate.
fields.example: Kitchen fire, sponge test run on a 1 ft x 1 ft square in each room; residue logged as wet smoke on the kitchen ceiling. Chris says wet smoke takes 4 to 6 times longer to clean than dry smoke, so kitchen cleaning labor is bid at the 5x midpoint [Encircle — 33iGNdZ6fyE @ 00:32:46].

fields.name: packout_photo_inventory
fields.prompt: Describe how every packed item on this job is captured in a digital photo inventory before it leaves the house. Note who shoots the photos, how boxes are labeled, and how fragile or oversized pieces are wrapped for the pod.
fields.example: Every item photographed before boxing, because a digital photo inventory protects against fraudulent claims and misplaced contents [Omegasonics — 3UmvqUcOFDc @ 00:01:09]. The floor mirror gets its 3-piece legs unscrewed and boxed in custom cardboard, the mirror blanketed, the legs shrink-wrapped to it and a fragile sticker added, since the loaded pod tilts high [FirehouseEducation — Appti0ctcGA @ 00:04:17].

fields.name: packing_materials_billing
fields.prompt: List every packing material used on the packout and state how each one is billed, either hourly or built into the per-box price. Flag any place where the crew skimped on materials because they assumed the cost was unrecoverable.
fields.example: Bubble wrap, moving blankets, shrink wrap and custom cardboard all logged on the packout sheet. Bubble wrap is billed at twenty dollars a box, and the crew lead is told not to skimp [FirehouseEducation — rAAR3Zmm80c @ 00:01:53]. Every case piece is fully shrink-wrapped with blankets on the corners before transit [FirehouseEducation — Appti0ctcGA @ 00:03:15].

fields.name: odor_method_selection
fields.prompt: Choose the deodorization method for each area and material on this fire job, ozone or hydroxyl, and justify the choice. Record which items are damp, wet, soft goods or leather, and how you will handle laundry from the house.
fields.example: No ozone on the damp sectional or the leather recliner, because ozone bleaches items and takes years off leather [FirehouseEducation — MkCNqNRsk04 @ 00:06:22]. Hydroxyl runs inside the drying chamber to deodorize. Laundry goes to a certified vendor, never the homeowner, since home washing obscures the source of any remaining odor [FirehouseEducation — MkCNqNRsk04 @ 00:09:05].

fields.name: afd_sizing
fields.prompt: Size the air filtration devices for the fire-damaged rooms using air changes per hour and particle counts. Record the starting particle count, the target count, the number of AFDs placed, and when you will step the air changes down.
fields.example: Living room and hallway sized for 6-8 air changes per hour at startup, dropping to 4 once counts fall. Opening particle count logged at 100,000; target is 2,000 particles at 3 microns, matching the 100,000 to 2,000 drop Chris cites when sizing AFDs with a particle counter [Encircle — 33iGNdZ6fyE @ 01:36:28]. Daily counts go in the job file.

fields.name: scan_capture_protocol
fields.prompt: Write the scan capture protocol your technicians follow on water and fire losses. Specify scan spacing, camera height, when pre-scans and post-scans happen, and how tight spaces such as bathrooms and under-sink cabinets get covered without blind spots.
fields.example: Scans placed 5-8 ft apart with the camera at about 4-4.5 ft [Adjuster TV — 86mEe0yHwiw @ 00:13:42]. Pre-scan before mitigation, post-scan after demolition, so the adjuster compares removed versus needed repair [Adjuster TV — 86mEe0yHwiw @ 00:06:43]. Under-sink loss: tripod at lowest height, cabinets open, plus 2 to 3 extra bathroom scans [Adjuster TV — 86mEe0yHwiw @ 00:23:01].

fields.name: written_notices_and_authority
fields.prompt: Record every written notice this job requires before work proceeds. Cover discard decisions on owner belongings, documented humidity when stabilization was refused, and no-warranty notices on heat-damaged materials, including who received each notice, when it went out, and how it was delivered.
fields.example: Owner decides on every discard; the crew has no authority to throw people's stuff out [Encircle — 33iGNdZ6fyE @ 01:20:22]. Carrier refused stabilization, so thermo-hygrometer readings went to the adjuster in writing [Encircle — 33iGNdZ6fyE @ 01:58:57]. Heat-damaged PEX no-warranty notice emailed to homeowner and adjuster on day two, homeowner as decision maker [Encircle — 33iGNdZ6fyE @ 03:49:52].

fields.name: plumber_discovery_profile
fields.prompt: Profile one service plumber you are pursuing. Record what they actually want from a restoration partner, how you found that out before pitching anything, their fee band in your CRM, and the jobs they have sent in the last 90 days.
fields.example: Rule one: find out what they want and give it to them [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — D4BavFC6d1E @ 00:01:28]. Plumber wants fast callbacks and a Category 2 versus Category 3 cheat sheet [Marketing Ninjas — n7ECptsaJTQ @ 00:03:13]. Two jobs sent in 60 days; one more within 90 days hits Shane's three-job referral-tree threshold [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — xXe9Z763dDc @ 00:12:23].

fields.name: free_dryout_ledger
fields.prompt: Track every free dry-out you have run for referring plumbers against the claims those plumbers converted. Record the current conversion ratio, the job-board label used, the drying protocol applied, and whether containment stayed under 90 minutes with no plumber charge.
fields.example: Three free dry-outs this quarter against twelve converted claims holds the 4:1 ratio [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — D4BavFC6d1E @ 00:12:00]. Each one is labeled 'water – free dryout' on the job board and run top-down instead of hammers. Doorway drying chamber built in under 90 minutes, and the plumber was never charged a dime [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — ufmHlZ6tfKg @ 00:02:04].

fields.name: call_conversion_system
fields.prompt: Map how an inbound water call is answered and converted on your team. Record the tracking whisper used, the promised arrival window, the callback time on missed calls, and your measured close rate against the benchmark for a working sales system.
fields.example: CallRail whisper announces the lead source before hello, arrival promised under 60 minutes, and missed calls returned within 3 to 5 minutes. Close rate measured at 64 percent last month, under the 75-80% benchmark, which Albi says signals a missing system [Restoration Success Strategies | Albi — mq8qI2hag0I @ 00:00:22]. The close process gets rebuilt this week.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 4 is complete only when the smoke type and multiplier are recorded, every packed item sits in a photo inventory, odor methods exclude ozone on damp, wet and soft goods, written notices are logged with recipients, the free dry-out ledger holds a 4:1 ratio, and the measured close rate is compared against 75-80%.

worksheets.title: Launching the Company: Contracts, Paid Leads, Margin and Assignment of Benefits
worksheets.purpose: Set up a restoration launch around a narrow emergency mitigation wedge, signed paper before any estimate, controlled paid leads and margin-based pricing, then handle assignments of benefits so they protect receivables without crossing into the inflation and kickback patterns that drove Florida reform.
instructions: Complete the launch fields before spending on ads or equipment, using your real purchasing power, referral source and target margin rather than hoped-for numbers.
Hold the paper gate: the signed agreement is in hand before any estimate is written, and there are no free estimates.
Answer every LSA call live, mark qualified calls booked even when lost, and lower budgets instead of pausing campaigns.
Before relying on any assignment, confirm coverage, deliver the contract before the crew arrives, and check font size and cancellation terms.
Compare every submitted invoice line for line against the first signed estimate, and record any referral payment so nothing is hidden from the homeowner.

fields.name: startup_capital_and_wedge
fields.prompt: State your total purchasing power, including loans, and the single referral source you are launching with. Describe the service wedge you will run first and the revenue point at which you plan to bring rebuild work in-house.
fields.example: Purchasing power is $120K, mostly an equipment loan, inside Albi's $50-200K range, with one plumbing company as the referral source [Restoration Success Strategies | Albi — 3PlUwHvZkxE @ 00:00:00]. Launch runs emergency water mitigation only for its 70%+ gross margins, referring rebuilds to a GC for a 10% kickback until revenue reaches $3-5M [Restoration Success Strategies | Albi — 3PlUwHvZkxE @ 00:03:12].

fields.name: signed_paper_before_estimate
fields.prompt: Describe the agreement package that gets signed before any estimate is written. List the termination fee, equipment minimums, and other protective terms it carries, and explain how this paper prevents a homeowner from taking the check and going silent.
fields.example: Signed work authorization in hand before any estimate, and no free estimates [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — b1-Dcqk4F9g @ 00:02:15]. Terms carry a 20% termination fee and a three-day equipment minimum. Shane frames the package as $5,000 worth of agreements for under 50 bucks [Shane O'Dazier | RestorationProfits — b1-Dcqk4F9g @ 00:00:46]. Homeowner initials the termination clause.

fields.name: lsa_lead_economics
fields.prompt: Record your Google Local Services Ads cost per lead and compare it with the regional ranges operators report. Note your state, weekly budget, how many qualified calls were marked booked, and what you will do instead of pausing the campaign.
fields.example: Texas account at $430 per lead, inside the $400-500 band Vinnie Mac reports for CA, FL, NY and TX [Water Damage Restoration Marketing - Vinnie Mac — 2akNGTmJry8 @ 00:32:17]. Every qualified call marked booked, even lost jobs. Slow weeks drop budget to $30, never pausing, since restarting acts as a reset [Water Damage Restoration Marketing - Vinnie Mac — O0STLVhCL2c @ 00:41:54].

fields.name: phone_answer_gate
fields.prompt: Describe who answers every paid-lead call, during which hours, and how the lead source is announced before the greeting. Confirm that no voicemail or AI answering service ever touches an LSA call, and name the backup when the primary is unavailable.
fields.example: Office manager answers live 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., owner's cell after hours; no voicemail and no AI service, because one or two missed calls kill a profile [Water Damage Restoration Marketing - Vinnie Mac — 2akNGTmJry8 @ 00:35:15]. Tracking number whisper says 'Google Local Service' before hello [Water Damage Restoration Marketing - Vinnie Mac — 2akNGTmJry8 @ 00:28:28].

fields.name: search_terms_and_service_area
fields.prompt: Record the keyword and service-area decisions on your emergency search campaigns. State whether terms like cost and cheap are negated or kept live, how wide your service area runs, and how you will judge whether the setting is working.
fields.example: Kept 'cost' and 'cheap' live instead of negating them; Restoration Growth Co calls that the best term in the whole account [Restoration Growth Co — zkR_04H9hBQ @ 00:07:41]. Service area set wider rather than narrow, following Vinnie Mac [Water Damage Restoration Marketing - Vinnie Mac — IDqwheOOgb0 @ 00:27:59]. Judged by booked qualified calls after thirty days.

fields.name: margin_and_landing_budget
fields.prompt: Convert your target gross margin into the markup you actually need and write the landing budget for one live job. Show job cost, target margin, required price, and the checkpoint where you will catch the job sliding.
fields.example: An $8,000 cost job at a 30% margin needs a 43% markup, or $3,440, not the 30% that dollar-thinkers add [Roofing Insights — ppn4akh1gPo @ 00:02:55]. Landing budget written before work starts: $11,440 price, labor capped at $4,100, checked at demo complete, because a sliding job cannot be caught without one [George Gabriel — KnWhJDOPsTc @ 00:02:28].

fields.name: florida_timeline_map
fields.prompt: For any Florida claim, map the pay-or-deny clock against the lien window and identify how many days remain for appraisal, mediation, or litigation. Note whether a direction to pay or letter of protection is in place instead of an assignment.
fields.example: Loss reported March 3; the 60-day pay-or-deny clock and the 90-day lien window leave roughly 30 days for appraisal, mediation, or litigation [Contractor Talk Podcast — Tg526FvHOmY @ 00:19:47]. Direction to pay signed in place of an AOB. A letter of protection puts the lien on insurance proceeds instead of the home [Contractor Talk Podcast — Tg526FvHOmY @ 00:42:17].

fields.name: aob_coverage_and_delivery_check
fields.prompt: Before relying on any assignment of benefits, confirm the loss is covered and the contract was delivered before the crew arrived. Record the delivery method, font size check, cancellation window, and how the split between mitigation and reconstruction change orders is handled.
fields.example: Coverage confirmed with the carrier first, since a correct denial leaves no rights to assign [magicplan — F4WLuIxWd-Q @ 00:14:03]. Hard copy delivered the night before, at 10-point font or larger for California [Claims Underground Podcast — bPBmUaKay2w @ 00:23:05]. 20-business-day cancellation clause. Mitigation sits under the assignment; reconstruction upgrades go on change orders.

fields.name: aob_abuse_red_flags
fields.prompt: List the abuse red flags you screen for on assignment jobs, your own and competitors'. Compare first estimate to submitted invoice, check for undisclosed referral payments, and record how you will keep your files clear of the patterns regulators cite.
fields.example: Red flag one: an $8,000 first estimate became a $22,000 invoice with mitigation the homeowner did not remember [The Fine Print — UxKcyrt-VS0 @ 00:01:05]. Red flag two: $1,000 to $2,000 cash plumber kickbacks undisclosed to the homeowner [Floridians For Honest Lending — I-S4L6YL2wo @ 00:02:18]. Our invoices must match the signed estimate line for line.

fields.name: receivables_and_misdirected_checks
fields.prompt: Describe how you protect receivables when an assignment is in place. Record the date the carrier received notice, what you do if the carrier still pays the homeowner, your payment terms, and how loss-draft delays are built into cash planning.
fields.example: Carrier notified of the assignment on day one by email. When they paid the homeowner anyway, we showed they knew and demanded a new check [magicplan — F4WLuIxWd-Q @ 00:15:32]. Terms avoid five-day payment demands, because nothing happens in five days in this industry [Claims Underground Podcast — bPBmUaKay2w @ 00:27:04]. Loss-draft delays budgeted at three months.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 5 is complete only when purchasing power and the launch wedge are written down, the signed agreement precedes every estimate, LSA calls are answered live, a landing budget exists for a live job, Florida timelines are mapped, and every assignment has confirmed coverage, advance delivery and an invoice that matches the signed estimate.

worksheets.title: Deductibles, Claim Checks, Claim Law and Storm Roofing Economics
worksheets.purpose: Keep every deductible, mortgage check and assignment on the right side of the law, then run storm roofing on evidence: a policy read before any promise, a repeatable hail photo set, a slope-by-slope repair-versus-replace decision, margin-based pricing and a clean self-checked estimate before submission.
instructions: Read the policy and calculate the deductible before promising the homeowner anything about the roof or the money.
Reject any deductible arrangement that bills the carrier a number the client was never charged, and record only the legal options you reviewed.
Build the mortgage packet with a contract precise enough that no servicer claim handler has to guess amounts or scope, and follow up on a set schedule.
Shoot the same photo set in the same elevation order on every hail claim, and run the repair-versus-replace worksheet slope by slope.
Price from margin, verify subcontractor coverage, and run a print-preview self-check before any estimate leaves the office.

fields.name: deductible_math_and_disclosure
fields.prompt: Calculate the deductible on this policy, including any percentage or wind and hail rider, and record how you explained it to the homeowner. Confirm in writing that the homeowner pays the deductible and that nobody is waiving or eating it.
fields.example: Dwelling limit $500,000 with a 2% deductible equals $10,000, owed the same on a $12,000 loss or a total loss [AnnePullen — tLwSSUZ6Awc @ 00:00:55]. Homeowner told that a contractor offering to make the deductible disappear is usually inflating the estimate [AnnePullen — tLwSSUZ6Awc @ 00:01:39]. Signed deductible acknowledgment filed with the contract.

fields.name: legal_deductible_coverage_options
fields.prompt: If the homeowner needs help covering the deductible, record only the legal options you reviewed. Note which coverages are ACV only with non-recoverable depreciation, any trades subcontracted back to the owner, and confirm no invoice will misstate the charge.
fields.example: Other structures paid ACV only, with bracketed non-recoverable depreciation, so that money is reviewed before agreeing to any deductible-only scope [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — DmesIP8hcak @ 00:22:33]. Owner takes back the gutter trade directly. No invoice bills the carrier a number the client was never charged, which Chad calls a felony [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — DmesIP8hcak @ 00:32:12].

fields.name: mortgage_check_packet
fields.prompt: Assemble the loss draft packet for any check naming the mortgage company. List the W-9, lien waivers, contract, and inspection items requested, the claim amount against the lender's no-holdback threshold, and your follow-up schedule with the servicer.
fields.example: Claim is $18,400, above the under-$10,000 no-holdback line, so an inspection is expected [Richard Levisee — VFWDHse67ws @ 00:06:48]. Packet holds W-9, lien waiver, and a contract precise enough that no claim handler guesses scope [Richard Levisee — VFWDHse67ws @ 00:03:44]. Follow-up call every Tuesday, since servicers simply wait until someone calls [Richard Levisee — VFWDHse67ws @ 00:08:30].

fields.name: adjuster_meeting_posture
fields.prompt: Plan your posture for the adjuster meeting on this claim. Record what you will say instead of handing over your estimate, what you will send when your number is far from theirs, and how you will request reinspection.
fields.example: At the meeting: we were hired to perform all repairs you prescribe and are here for our marching orders, so the adjuster shows their cards first [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — DmesIP8hcak @ 00:39:21]. Numbers far apart, so an Xactimate photo report with no line items, two photos each page, forces reinspection [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — DmesIP8hcak @ 00:41:19].

fields.name: aob_validity_check
fields.prompt: If an assignment of benefits is part of this claim, confirm it is a true assignment rather than a direction to pay, and that every named insured signed. Record what the homeowner was told about losing control of the claim money.
fields.example: Document reviewed: a true assignment, signed by both named insureds [Butler Legal — rxahzd6qaCw @ 00:06:17]. Homeowner told that with an AOB assigned to the contractor, the money is now in the contractor's possession, not theirs [Crossroads Insurance Recovery — iKLGuESx4po @ 00:03:42], and that a prevailing assignee can request attorney's fees [Butler Legal — rxahzd6qaCw @ 00:17:02].

fields.name: policy_read_before_promise
fields.prompt: Read the policy before promising the homeowner anything about the roof. Record the roof endorsement, any ACV roof language, prior roof payments, and the questions the client emailed to their own agent about limits, depreciation, and cosmetic exclusions.
fields.example: Policy checked for PPRC, a 400R ACV roof endorsement on the newly replaced roof, and a $27,000 roof check two years back [Adjuster TV — 6084H_VeZTA @ 00:22:05]. Client emailed their agent asking about O&L limits, ACV versus RCV, and cosmetic or marring exclusions, since the contractor cannot discuss policy [Chad Michael - The Practitioner — Op9Qkl-qW58 @ 00:05:39].

fields.name: hail_inspection_photo_set
fields.prompt: Document the hail inspection on this roof as a repeatable photo set. Record the elevation order you walked, the number of roof and total photos, how test squares were placed, and when you stopped counting hits on each square.
fields.example: Elevations walked front, right, rear, left, same order every claim; 42 roof photos and 108 total, inside Matt's 30-50 and 90-120 ranges [Adjuster TV — 6084H_VeZTA @ 01:03:52]. Test square placed away from the contractor's square, never on top of it, and counting stopped at 10 hits [Adjuster TV — 6084H_VeZTA @ 01:00:12].

fields.name: repair_vs_replace_worksheet
fields.prompt: Run the repair-versus-replace decision slope by slope. Record the per-shingle repair value, the per-square replacement value, the count of damaged shingles on each slope, and which slopes you are writing for replacement versus repair, with reasons.
fields.example: Haag-based worksheet values: $24.80 per shingle against $368.78 per square, vents excluded [Claim Daddy — yytgxtBGSF8 @ 00:26:11]. Rear and left slopes written for replacement; right slope repaired with 22 shingles. Clustered marks were flagged, because frequent contractor damage tends to be non-random [Claim Daddy — yytgxtBGSF8 @ 00:30:46].

fields.name: price_per_square_and_margin
fields.prompt: Check the scope price per square and your margin-based sell price before ordering the build. Record the carrier's price per square, your job cost, the price at cost divided by 0.65, and any gap you must close through supplementing.
fields.example: Scope pays $205 per square, near the $190 Bensman calls unprofitable and below his $250-$450 target [The STRONG Roofer w/ Adam Bensman — -aZHNsY5qIY @ 00:04:06]. Job cost $10,000, so margin price is $15,384, not $13,500 at 1.35 markup, which leaves you short almost $2,000 [RoofCoach — gLFs8l5O0j4 @ 00:02:17]. Supplement targets the gap.

fields.name: sub_crew_and_submission_check
fields.prompt: Before the first nail and before submitting the estimate, record the subcontractor's workers comp and GL verification, your supervision plan for early jobs, the count of unpaid jobs outstanding, and the results of your print-preview self-check.
fields.example: Sub's workers comp and GL verified active this morning; owner stays on the roof for the first three jobs to catch 2-nail shortcuts [Digital Roofing Innovations — tVMI8UScmmE @ 00:00:20]. Two unpaid jobs open, under the limit of three [Roofing Insights — FqdbOCycivo @ 00:04:18]. Print preview caught a missing deductible and a stray grouping note [Adjuster TV — lIyYVIMZa0s @ 00:08:16].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 6 is complete only when the deductible is calculated and acknowledged in writing, no arrangement misstates a charge, the mortgage packet and follow-up schedule exist, any assignment is verified as true and fully signed, the policy was read before promises, and the hail photo set, slope decisions, margin price, sub coverage and self-check are all recorded.
